family: # Redstone-tick families (clk-rt, NOTES: designs/clocks/tracks/clk-rt/NOTES.md). "redstone-tick" = every changing block is a redstone_torch, repeater, comparator or redstone_wire.

why: A torch, repeater or comparator changes state (block state or comparator strength) only in its own scheduled tick, scheduled >= 2 gt ahead, and a position holds at most one pending tick of its block (LevelChunkTicks.schedule refuses a second (pos, block) pair): two changes of one component are >= 2 gt apart, so one on/off cycle takes >= 4 gt. Dust only follows them inside the tick. P 1, 2 or 3 needs a component changing twice within 2 gt.

family: any redstone-tick family, self-starting or kicked at an even tick
why: Every delay is even (torch 2, comparator 2, repeater 2/4/6/8, burnout re-check 160, dust 0) and the placement's updates all happen between two ticks: every change happens at placement + even and pending ticks keep that parity, so the states at t and t + odd differ unless nothing is pending. Odd periods need a kick at an odd tick (`port start: ... at N`): P5 ring and P205 burnout exist that way.

A torch in the active set turns off at least once per period; with P <= 8 its 8th turn-off comes within 7P <= 56 <= 60 gt of the first: RedstoneTorchBlock.isToggledTooFrequently burns it out and it stays dark >= 160 gt (re-check) -- not periodic with P. (Burnout clocks use exactly this: P220, P205.)

A torch strongly powers only the block directly above it (RedstoneTorchBlock.getDirectSignal: UP only; its weak signal reaches dust and diodes, never a plain block beside it), and a torch reads only the block it hangs or stands on: a torch's input is a torch one level lower, so the dependencies never loop and every torch settles. (A ring needs one dust or diode to come back down: the 3-torch dust ring P12 has 14 blocks.)
Dust never schedules a tick: its power is recomputed inside the update that changed a neighbor, so without a torch, repeater or comparator nothing is pending after placement and the state is fixed.

family: # One row per (family, unreachable periods), with the proof: a reason read in the game's source, or an exhaustive census. The catalog shows these rows ("Periods a family cannot reach"). Track clk-obs wrote the first two (2026-10-19); P3 for this family is still OPEN: see designs/clocks/tracks/clk-obs/NOTES.md (necessary structure: only pistons 0-ticking every 3 gt can change; none with <= 5 blocks, exhaustive census).

why: The period is the smallest P with the whole state at tick t+P equal to the state at tick t, sampled once per game tick: a period of 1 means the sampled state never changes, so there is no signal (sub-tick activity, e.g. 0-tick pulses, is invisible at that sampling).

family: block-update clocks: any family made only of observer, piston, sticky_piston, redstone_block, redstone_lamp, copper_bulb, note_block, trapdoors, doors, fence gates, rails (no dust, torch, repeater, comparator, sculk, hopper, dropper, leaves or scaffolding)
why: Every component that changes has its own period >= 3, and a clock's period is a common multiple of its components' periods. Observer >= 4 (ObserverBlock.tick: off -> on schedules the next tick 2 gt later, on -> off; updateShape/startSignal schedule a tick only when unpowered with none pending, always 2 gt ahead: on exactly 2 gt, off >= 2 gt). Piston >= 3 (a retracting base is a moving_piston for 2 gt and lands in the block-entity phase, after the block events, so a powered piston extends again at the earliest the next tick: extend at t, retract at t' >= t, extend again >= t'+3). Lamp >= 5 (RedstoneLampBlock: lit in the powering update, unlit only by its 4 gt tick scheduled at the first unpowered update: lit >= 4 gt). Copper bulb: lit toggles only on rising edges of its power, and that power comes from the components above (periods >= 3), so it cannot change with period 1 or 2 either; note blocks, trapdoors, doors, gates and rails copy their power and emit none; redstone blocks, slime and plain blocks move only when a piston moves them. So nothing can change with period 1 or 2. (P = 3 would need every changing component to be a piston 0-ticking every 3 gt: observers, lamps and bulbs could not take part.)

family: every family, small (the census's full palette: every modeled component needing no item or entity, ~100 states; self-start or one block placed last)
periods: 2, 3 with <= 4 blocks in 2x2x1, 2x1x2, 3x2x1, 3x1x2, 2x2x2, 3x3x1, 3x2x2, 3x1x3 and <= 3 blocks in 3x3x2
why: Exhaustive census on redsim (clockinfra, 2026-10-19): `mctas clock census --palette full --max-period 3 --warmup 60 --box B --k K` finds 0 clocks in each of these boxes (a candidate is dropped when its whole state does not repeat within 12 gt; the same runs with --max-period 4 find the known P4 clocks, so the pruning keeps real ones). Bigger designs are not covered by this row.
